html:
Walvis Bay is a port town on the Atlantic coast of Namibia, held by Britain and then South Africa as a small enclave from 1878 to 1994. The map shows it in its 1938 snapshot.

Its natural harbour is the best on that desert coast. Britain annexed it in 1878, and it became part of the Cape Colony in 1884, just as Germany claimed the land around it as German South West Africa. The Germans built their own port at Swakopmund nearby instead.

After South Africa conquered the German colony in 1915, Walvis Bay was run as part of South West Africa from 1922. When Namibia became independent in 1990, South Africa kept the enclave. It was handed over to Namibia in 1994.
